page: Microsoft Azure M96ds_1_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory footprints and high parallel processing capability. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 974.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 10.15 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage configuration includes 429 GB of local SSD capacity, suitable for transient scratch spaces, swap files, or local caching layers. The instance is also Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with persistent high-performance remote disk options. No discrete GPUs are provisioned with this model, focusing computational resources strictly on CPU and high-density memory operations.

From an architectural standpoint, the allocation of over 10 GB of RAM per vCPU places this machine firmly in the memory-heavy category. The qualitative cost profile reflects its enterprise scale: provisioning dedicated hardware slices of this magnitude incurs a substantial operational commitment, balanced by high density that reduces node fragmentation in clustered database environments. Tradeoffs include a relatively modest local scratch SSD volume relative to the total RAM footprint, necessitating remote storage configurations for durable large-scale data sets.

Workload applicability centers on large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, relational database systems including Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle, distributed memory caching clusters, and high-concurrency enterprise batch transaction systems requiring near-instantaneous memory retrieval.
